context: Data visualization — parallel coordinates chart of 300 synthetic employees across 6 mixed-scale axes (linear, log, ordinal), with brushable filtering and department color encoding.
first_impression: Competent and functional parallel coordinates with deliberate palette choices, but the mass of crossing lines overwhelms the ordinal axes and makes the unfiltered state feel busy rather than informative.
what_works: Deliberate use of the Tol colorblind-safe palette instead of schemeCategory10 shows real color intentionality; dual-pass canvas rendering (0.04 alpha inactive, 0.30 active) and the monospace filter counter are thoughtful implementation details. Axis sublabels ('log scale', 'years', '1–5 rating') add useful context without visual clutter.
what_doesnt: The ordinal Department and Education axes concentrate all 300 lines into a handful of discrete y-positions, creating dense bundles that obscure any pattern — a layout consequence that isn't mitigated by curve smoothing, jitter, or axis reordering hints. At the rendered size the subtitle text ('2 linear, 1 log, 2 ordinal, 1 linear scale') reads as a developer note rather than a user-facing label, and the tight 36px horizontal margins leave little breathing room between the axes and the chart edges.
